bib.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, Long Beach, California, PMLR 97, 2019

question: Can a pre-trained text Transformer be adapted to many downstream tasks by training only a few added parameters per task, without losing accuracy relative to full fine-tuning?
hypothesis: Small bottleneck adapter modules with near-identity initialisation inside a frozen BERT match full fine-tuning at a fraction of the per-task parameters.
contributions: Bottleneck adapter module and its integration into Transformer layers
Near full fine-tuning accuracy on GLUE and 17 further classification tasks with 1-4% task parameters
Ablation of which layers' adapters matter and robustness to size and init scale

method.summary: Insert two serial bottleneck adapters per Transformer layer of a frozen BERT, train only adapters, layer norms and the classifier per task, and compare with full and top-layer fine-tuning on GLUE, 17 classification tasks and SQuAD v1.1.
method.task: text classification and extractive QA transfer

datasets.name: GLUE (excl. WNLI)
datasets.split: test via GLUE server; validation for selection

datasets.name: 17 additional text classification tasks
datasets.size: 900 to 330k train examples; 2 to 157 classes; avg length 57 to 1.9k chars
datasets.source: 20 newsgroups, Crowdflower, customer complaint (catalog.data.gov), news aggregator, SMS spam

models.name: Adapter module
models.params: 2md + d + m per adapter (incl. biases); 0.5-8% of model
models.architecture: down-project d->m, nonlinearity, up-project m->d, internal skip; two per Transformer layer (after attention projection, after feed-forward), before the skip add and layer norm
models.init_from: random, near-identity: zero-mean Gaussian std 1e-2 truncated to 2 std

other.also_trained: layer norm params and classifier layer; base frozen

models.name: AutoML no-BERT baseline
models.architecture: feedforward/conv nets on TF-Hub text embeddings
models.init_from: TF Hub embeddings, frozen or tuned

training.objective: supervised task loss; linear classifier on [CLS] embedding (SQuAD span selection)
training.lr: GLUE sweep {3e-5,3e-4,3e-3}; other tasks {1e-5,3e-5,1e-4,3e-3}; SQuAD FT {3e-5,5e-5,1e-4}, adapters {3e-5,1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup over first 10% of steps, then linear decay to zero
training.epochs: GLUE {3,20}; other tasks {20,50,100} chosen manually (Table 4); SQuAD FT {2,3,5}, adapters {3,10,20}
training.seeds: GLUE: 5 seeds, best on validation; Fig 4/5/7 three seeds; Table 2 mean +- s.e.m. over seeds (count not stated)

metrics.name: GLUE score
metrics.definition: MRPC and QQP F1, STS-B Spearman, CoLA Matthews correlation, others accuracy; Total is the mean

metrics.name: Total num params / trained params per task
metrics.definition: model size across all tasks as multiple of BERT; share of parameters trained per task

baselines: Variable fine-tuning (top n layers, n in {1,2,3,5,7,9,11,12})
AutoML no-BERT baseline (30 CPU machines, one week per task)
eval.protocol: Hyperparameter sweep per dataset and method; best model on validation; GLUE test via server; GLUE re-run 5 seeds.

results.claim: Adapter tuning of BERT-large reaches a mean GLUE test score of 80.0 against 80.4 for full fine-tuning, with 3.6% trained parameters per task.
results.setup: BERT-large (24 layers, 330M), GLUE test via server, adapter size chosen per task from {8,64,256}, best of 5 seeds on validation
results.quote: Adapters achieve a mean GLUE score of 80.0, compared to 80.4 achieved by full

results.claim: Total parameters to solve the 9 GLUE tasks: 1.3x BERT for adapters vs 9x for fine-tuning.
results.table: Table 1, row Adapters (8-256), column Total num params

results.claim: Fixing adapter size to 64 on GLUE gives a mean score of 79.6 with 2.1% trained parameters per task.
results.setup: BERT-large, adapter size 64 for all tasks
results.quote: leads to a small decrease in average accuracy to 79.6

results.claim: On 17 additional classification tasks (BERT-base) adapters average 73.3 vs 73.7 for full fine-tuning, with 1.14% new parameters per task and 1.19x total.
results.setup: BERT-base, 17 tasks, test accuracy, mean over seeds

results.claim: Variable fine-tuning (top n layers) averages 74.0 on the additional tasks, above full fine-tuning (73.7), training 52.9% of parameters on average.
results.table: Table 2, row Average, column Variable FT

results.claim: AutoML no-BERT baseline averages 72.7 on the additional tasks, below all BERT variants.
results.setup: One week on 30 CPU machines per task, over 10k models on average
results.table: Table 2, row Average, column No BERT baseline

results.claim: Fine-tuning only the top layer of BERT-base on MNLI-m gets 77.8% validation accuracy with about 9M trainable parameters, vs 83.7% for size-64 adapters with about 2M and 84.4% for full fine-tuning.
results.setup: BERT-base, MNLI-m validation, mean +- s.e.m. over seeds
